The scrape ran six feet long under a dead spruce, dug to the frozen dirt and floored with cut boughs. The fallen trunk roofed it. Snow-loaded limbs closed the gaps.
The bark split down a channel. A figure stepped out through the split, and the wood closed behind her without a seam.
Gray skin, grained like weathered heartwood, with darker channels running up the outsides of her arms. Her face ran smooth where her arms ran grained. Her fingers ran a joint too long and ended in points. She wore nothing. No fog came off her mouth in the cold.
Ovrik got the crossbow up crosswise. The axe came down over the stock. Ovrik turned his body into the swing, and the edge missed the join of his neck by a hand's width and struck across his ribs. The leather turned the arc partway. Blood came out fast and dark. It ran down inside his belt, steamed at the lips of the cut, and soaked the wool black.
Darric hauled the axe back over his shoulder. His cheeks hung slack. His brows sat level. His mouth stayed closed and easy. Below the collar his chest heaved and his boots dug for the next drive.
Red spotted the gray snow behind his boots, a drop to a step. Merra's finger took up the slack.
